{{recipe}}

Tired of the same old stews? This '''spicy chicken stew''' will have your taste buds jumping right off your tongue!

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] boneless skinless [[Cookbook:Chicken#Leg|chicken thighs]], cut into 1 ½-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] cubes
* [[Cookbook:Flour|Flour]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Rapeseed Oil|canola oil]]
* 1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* ¼ cup red [[Cookbook:Curry Paste|curry paste]]
* 5 Thai [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]], stemmed
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|fish sauce]]
* 1 cup chicken [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]]
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 4 red [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], cut into 2-inch cubes
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* [[Cookbook:Chopping|Chopped]] [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]

== Procedure ==
#[[Cookbook:Dredging|Dredge]] chicken in flour. Set aside.
#Heat oil in a 6-[[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] cast-iron [[Cookbook:Dutch Oven|Dutch oven]]. Add 6 chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides. Repeat until all chicken has been browned, then remove from pot.
#[[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] onion in remaining oil until translucent and slightly browned around edges. Mix in the curry paste, chiles, fish sauce, broth, tomato paste, potatoes, and garlic.
#Return the chicken to the pot. Cover tightly and place in 250°F [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] for 4½ hours, or until chicken is cooked through and tender.
#Sprinkle individual serving bowls with chopped parsley and serve warm.

steps.text: Dredge chicken in flour. Set aside.
Heat oil in a 6-quart cast-iron Dutch oven. Add 6 chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides. Repeat until all chicken has been browned, then remove from pot.
Sauté onion in remaining oil until translucent and slightly browned around edges. Mix in the curry paste, chiles, fish sauce, broth, tomato paste, potatoes, and garlic.
Return the chicken to the pot. Cover tightly and place in 250°F oven for 4½ hours, or until chicken is cooked through and tender.
Sprinkle individual serving bowls with chopped parsley and serve warm.
